name: Chamber of Commerce Committee Liaison Meeting Agenda
minutes_text:
CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS
  455 North Rexford Drive
  Beverly Hills, CA 90210
  Video Teleconference
  Beverly Hills City Council Chamber of Commerce Liaison Committee Meeting

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Wednesday, June 12, 2024
  2:00 PM

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  June 12, 2024 / 2:02 PM
IN ATTENDANCE:  Mayor Lester Friedman, Councilmember Mary Wells, Assistant City
  Manager Ryan Gohlich, Community Outreach Manager Magdalena Davis,
  Beverly Hills Chamber of Commerce President & CEO Todd Johnson,
  Beverly Hills Chamber of Commerce Director of Economic Development &
  Government Affairs Brittany Ganson

  1) Public Comment:
  a. David by Zoom: He notices that the hourly rate for high level members of the
  chamber such as the COO and CEO have stagnated since 2018. He is proposing
  that the hourly rates of these positions be increased.

  2) Beverly Hills Chamber of Commerce Workplan:
  a. Presentation by Brittany Ganson
  i. Update on Q3 & Q4 Fiscal 2023-2024 Programs & Initiatives
  1. The Chamber conducted several marketing and outreach events for
  the City, including Office Hours with Doctor Gold, 60 Second
  Shoutouts, Concours d’Elegance, Walk the Neighborhood, Parklet
  Outreach, Small Business Task Force outreach, and NOW BH
  Outreach.
  2. Other economic development and business support events
  assisted by the Chamber were the Property Owners Task Force,
  the Small Business Development Center, Broker’s Roundtables,
  the Small Business Task Force, Mayora Business Retention
  meetings, LA Metro Subway Stakeholder meetings, and the New
  Business Newsletter.
  3. The Chamber’s social media presence increased on both Facebook
  and Instagram during Q3 &Q4.
  4. The #SelfCareCity did not perform well, and the Chamber attributes
  this to the campaign not incorporating Beverly Hills Businesses and
  instead relying on more abstract concepts.
  5. The Chamber has decided to replace their old social media agency
  with PSM Communication Arts.
  6. PSM Communication Arts has worked with El Segundo, Redondo
  Beach, the Mexican Tourism Board, and the Metropolis
  development in Downtown LA.
 Highlights for June 12, 2024
Chamber of Commerce Liaison Committee

  7. PSM Communication Arts’ main critiques of NOW Beverly Hills is
  the lack of connection between the various campaigns.
  ii. Proposed Chamber FY 2024-2025 workplan.
  1. The Chamber has planned a number of marketing and outreach
  events for the upcoming year, including Les is More, Concours
  d’Elegance, the Holiday Lighting Celebration, and promotional
  materials such as eblasts, social media posts, weekly newsletters,
  and Walk the Neighborhood reports.
  2. The New York Business Attraction trip will hold 24 meetings in New
  York City over the course of three days, which will focus on
  attracting emerging new retail brands, high end restaurants, and
  entertainment/innovative professional services.
  3. Other economic development and business support items for the
  coming year are the Property Owners Task Force, the Small
  Business Development Center, Broker’s Roundtables, the Small
  Business Task Force, Mayora Business Retention meetings, LA
  Metro Subway Stakeholder meetings, and the New Business
  Newsletter.
  4. The Chamber proposed to have PSM Communication Arts run the
  2024-2025 Now Beverly Hills Shop Local program.
  5. The Chamber will also create new regional business attraction
  marketing materials in conjunction with Creative Agency.
  6. Miami Business Attraction research will be done in collaboration
  with UrbanCentric Analytics prior to the Miami Business Mission.
  7. The Miami Mission will have a five-point marketing strategy.
  a. Committing to creating a long-term highly visible presence
  in South Florida targeting social media accounts,
  businesses, and entrepreneurs.
  b. Telling the Beverly Hills Story: getting Beverly Hills into the
  minds of businesses and investors.
  c. ID growing businesses and South Florida’s most creative
  developers in the hospitality, restaurant, financial, and tech
  sectors.
  d. Recruit local businesses leaders as BH ambassadors.
  e. Hold visits with key organizations and leaders.
  8. The Miami Business Attraction Mission will consist of 3 days of
  approximately 18 business attraction meetings with a focus on the
  retail, restaurant, and entertainment sectors. This is expected to
  cost $100,000.
  9. In contrast, a trip with two meeting days would cost around $80,000
  and have approximately 12 meetings.
  10. The Chamber is also requesting four Special Event Fee Waivers
  and a flat fee parking rate for one event, with a total worth of
  approximately $43,000.
  11. The total work plan contract is $553,245.
  b. The Chamber feels that the revamping of Now Beverly Hills in conjunction with
  PSM Communication Arts will have an important impact on the marketing efforts
  of the business community.
  c. The research for the Miami trip in FY-2023-2024 cost $20,000.
  d. The San Francisco Business Attraction Mission was cancelled due to COVID and
  was deemed to unsafe to continue after.
 Highlights for June 12, 2024
Chamber of Commerce Liaison Committee
